name: @flarekit-dev/mcp

tools.name: flare.capabilities.list
tools.description:
List what this kit can do on the selected network, from the deployment registries. Distinguishes a capability confirmed by a live round trip from one that is merely deployed, names the tools that serve each, and declares the tools that are NOT built with the reason. Call this first to find out what is possible before planning anything.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

family.description: Restrict to one family, e.g. "ftso". Omit for every family.

tools.name: flare.feeds.list
tools.description:
List the FTSO price feeds this network actually publishes, with each feed's trust class. Enumerated live from the deployment, so it reflects governance changes. Use this to find the exact feed name before calling flare.feeds.get.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring, e.g. "USD". Omit to list every feed.

tools.name: flare.feeds.get
tools.description:
Read current FTSO values by feed name, with full precision, the quote asset and the protocol timestamp. Values carry their source and are never rounded.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

names.description: Feed names, e.g. ["FLR/USD", "BTC/USD"]. Call flare.feeds.list to discover them.

tools.name: flare.random.get
tools.description:
Read Flare's secure random number, current or for a past voting round. Refuses rather than returning a value the protocol has not marked secure, so an unusable answer cannot be mistaken for a usable one.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

votingRoundId.description: A historical voting round. Omit for the current random. Reaches back roughly 574 days on Coston2 — further than price history, so a round can have retrievable randomness and an unretrievable price at the same time.

allowInsecure.description: Accept a value the protocol has NOT marked secure. False by default and should stay false for anything a result depends on. Setting it true is a statement that this randomness is decorative.

tools.name: flare.operations.list
tools.description:
List the durable operations this server has recorded, newest first, with the state each one actually reached. Use it to see what is still in flight before starting anything new.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

open.description: Only operations that have not reached a final state.

tools.name: flare.operations.get
tools.description:
Read one operation in full: its state, its steps and the actor each is waiting on, the intent it was created from, and the evidence gathered so far.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

tools.name: flare.portfolio.get
tools.description:
Read balances and positions for an EVM and/or XRP Ledger identity, with per-chain coverage. A balance that could not be read is reported as absent with a reason, never as zero. Needs no key: the addresses are arguments.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

evm.description: An EVM address. Defaults to the agent account when one is configured.

xrpl.description: An XRP Ledger classic address. Omit if there is none to read.

tools.name: flare.tokens.list
tools.description:
List the tokens that can be swapped on this network, with the exact key to pass to flare.quote and flare.plan, and the decimals needed to express an amount. Call this before quoting if you do not already know the keys.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

tools.name: flare.tee.machines
tools.description:
List the active TEE machines registered on Flare Confidential Compute, with their proxy URLs. Reads the chain directly and needs no credentials.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

limit.description: How many machines to return. The full count is reported separately.

offset.description: Where to start in the active-machine list.

tools.name: flare.tee.machine
tools.description:
Read one TEE machine: its registration status, code hash, platform, and what is actually proven about it. Distinguishes a machine that is merely registered from one whose attestation was verified, because those are different claims.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

tools.name: flare.wallet.status
tools.description:
Report the agent account this server signs with: its address, its exact native balance, and whether it is funded. Read this before any write tool to see the blast radius. Never returns a private key.

Class: read. Observes state only, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

tools.name: flare.quote
tools.description:
Price a swap at the current pool state without composing or recording anything. Use this to compare options; use flare.plan when you have chosen one, because only a plan has an id that flare.execute will act on.

Class: plan. Prices or composes an unsigned, expiring artifact. Signs nothing, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

fromKey.description: Token key to spend, e.g. "FXRP". Call flare.tokens.list if you do not know it.

toKey.description: Token key to receive, e.g. "USDT0". Call flare.tokens.list if you do not know it.

amount.description: How much to spend, as a person writes it — "1.5". Preferred over amountIn.

amountIn.description: Raw units, if you already have them. Needing this means knowing the decimals and doing the arithmetic, so `amount` exists to avoid both.

slippageBips.description: Basis points below the quote the swap would still accept. 50 = 0.5%.

tools.name: flare.plan
tools.description:
Price an intent and compose an immutable, expiring plan with an id, persisted so it can be executed and reconciled later. Signs nothing and moves nothing. Pass the returned operationId to flare.execute to carry it out.

Class: plan. Prices or composes an unsigned, expiring artifact. Signs nothing, moves no value, and needs no key configured.

kind.description: The only intent kind with a complete quote-to-plan chain today. Other families are declared unbuilt in flare.capabilities.list rather than simulated here.

fromKey.description: Token key to spend, e.g. "FXRP". Call flare.tokens.list if you do not know it.

toKey.description: Token key to receive, e.g. "USDT0". Call flare.tokens.list if you do not know it.

amount.description: How much to spend, as a person writes it — "1.5". Preferred over amountIn.

amountIn.description: Raw units, if you already have them. Needing this means knowing the decimals and doing the arithmetic, so `amount` exists to avoid both.

slippageBips.description: The floor enforced by the router itself, in basis points. 50 = 0.5%.

account.description: Who would execute this plan. Defaults to the configured agent account. Supply it to plan for an address this server holds no key for.

tools.name: flare.execute
tools.description:
Execute a plan previously composed by flare.plan, by its operation id. Raises the allowance first if the plan says one is needed. Returns when the transaction is submitted — that is not the same as succeeded, and this tool never claims otherwise.

Class: write. MOVES VALUE and requires a configured signer.

operationId.description: The id returned by flare.plan. The terms come from the stored plan, not from here.

stderr: flarekit-mcp 1.0.0 on Flare Testnet Coston2 — 14 tools, 13 of them keyless.
